text:
ashley: Heads up — after merging PR #421 (provider split) the gpupool module started reconciling duplicate nodegroups across regions. Terraform apply returned success but cloud shows extra instance groups; billing alert fired.

raj: I saw that. Looks like provider aliasing got inconsistent between module and root. module was switched to using `provider = aws.alias` while some callsites still pass the legacy provider. Reconcile loop every gitops sync.

mira: Confirmed in the plan logs: we get create + delete every apply for the same logical gpupool. snippet: 
```
# plan excerpt
~ module.gpupool.aws_autoscaling_group.gpu (forces replacement)
  -/+ (config changed)
```

oliver: infra-bot shows three reconciles in the last hour: sync -> plan -> apply -> drift detected -> repeat. That explains the cost spike. @sre how bad was the billing blip?

sre: Cost alert: ~+$3.8k in the last 6 hours, mostly from duplicate GPU instances in us-west-2. We scaled the duplicates down manually but need a proper fix.

raj: Short term: avoid further creates by adding a provider-compat shim in calling modules. Eg, in gpupool module create a provider block that defaults to legacy provider if alias not provided. That prevents double-attach during rollout.

ashley: Agreed. Proposal: revert the provider-split PR in root while we ship a compatibility shim in the module and add an acceptance test. Revert should be quick to stop churn.

oliver: Also add a pre-apply CI gate that runs a guarded plan check to fail fast if there are unexpected `create` actions against gpupool resources in a different region. Example check: 
```
terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform show -json tfplan | jq '.resource_changes[] | select(.type=="aws_autoscaling_group" and .change.actions|index("create"))'
```

mira: Another thing — some callsites passed `provider = aws` via module call, others passed `providers = { aws = aws.west }`. That mismatch made terraform treat them as distinct. We should standardize on `providers = { aws = aws.<alias> }` and add a module variable `provider_alias` with default empty to preserve old behavior.

ci-bot: GitOps sync: repo/infra at commit 9a7b... detected drift: 2 created, 0 destroyed, 4 updated.

raj: To repair state: use `terraform state list` to find duplicates and `terraform state mv` to consolidate before any destroy. Do NOT run a destroy across both regions at once. Work with cloud team to cordon duplicated nodegroups first.

ashley: I'll open an emergency PR to add the shim + acceptance test + clear upgrade notes in the module README. Plan: revert root PR -> merge shim -> bump module minor -> then reapply provider split with a gradual rollout.

oliver: For longer term: add a module integration test in CI that runs against a mocked provider or small sandbox to ensure provider alias changes don't create resource churn. Also: add an automated budget guard to block merges that cause projected >$1k delta in 24h.

sre: Thanks. Paging cloud on the manual scale-down ops so we can fully remove the duplicates after state is reconciled.

ashley: FYI I'll tag people in the PR and include the terraform state mv steps. TL;DR: revert root provider-split in next 15m, then follow the compatibility-shim path. :pray: 

infra-bot: Action item created: INFRA-1123 (provider-split rollback + gpupool compatibility shim)

mira: I'll draft the shim snippet and test matrix. Will post before the revert completes.

ashley: perfect — thanks all.
